solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Straight there, mad with love (6)

indicators.note: the letters of THERE go crazy and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go straight over there, out of their mind with love.
explanation.walkthrough: "Straight" reads as "directly" beside "there", but it is the definition: straight in the sense of heterosexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is informal for heterosexual, and HETERO is its short form.

clue.text: Beg former husband to write regularly (6)

indicators.note: take every other letter, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Someone is told to plead with their ex-husband to keep in touch by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: "Former husband" looks like one unit, EX, but it splits: EX from "former", H from "husband".
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge or entreat someone, which is to beg them.

clue.text: Reissue film about food additives (11)

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A film about food additives is being put out again.
explanation.walkthrough: "Reissue" looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; "about" does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsifiers are added to food to keep oil and water mixed.

clue.text: Expose disagreeable church delegate (9)

blocks.note: to out someone is to expose them

explanation.surface: A newspaper reveals the misconduct of an unpleasant church representative.
explanation.walkthrough: "Delegate" reads as a noun, a person sent to a synod; it is the verb, to hand work to others.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsource work is to delegate it to an outside supplier.

clue.text: Thieves finally flee, clutching first-class artwork (8)

indicators.note: take the final letter of "Thieves"
ESCAPE holds the A in its grip

explanation.surface: Art thieves make a run for it holding a top-quality painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The heist story makes "artwork" look like the loot, but it is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting of the sea, a kind of artwork.

clue.text: Expert on board plane? (7)

blocks.note: riding the waves on a surfboard

explanation.surface: Is the skilled person on this flight a pilot?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about aircraft, but the board is a surfboard and a plane is a flat surface; a SURF ACE is an expert on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from geometry, where a plane is any flat two-dimensional expanse.

clue.text: At heart, Marx understood language of class (5)

indicators.note: take the heart, the middle letters, of MARX

explanation.surface: Deep down, Karl Marx grasped the jargon of class struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: With Marx in the clue, "class" means social class; argot is the slang of any particular group.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the special vocabulary of a particular group or class of people.

clue.text: Pass officer briefly (3)

indicators.note: use the short form of the officer's rank

blocks.note: a mountain pass, the dip in a ridge between peaks
the short written form of the rank Colonel

explanation.surface: An officer is quickly handed something, or waved through.
explanation.walkthrough: A col is the low point of a ridge between two peaks, where a route crosses; Col is also the standard abbreviation of Colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographer's word: the saddle between two summits is the natural pass over a range.

clue.text: Put books on top of American organ (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the earlier pieces sit above A

explanation.surface: Someone stacks books on top of an American's organ, the musical kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture suggests a church organ with music piled on it; the organ is the one that nourishes a baby in the womb.
explanation.definitionFit: The placenta is an organ that forms in the womb during pregnancy.

clue.text: Corrosion in the right rocket engine (8)

indicators.note: something that is in another sits inside it, so RUST goes inside THE

explanation.surface: Rust has got into the correct rocket motor.
explanation.walkthrough: "The right rocket engine" reads as one noun phrase, but THE and R are wordplay and only "rocket engine" defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A thruster is a small rocket engine used to steer a spacecraft.

clue.text: Introduction to Guinness, almost invariably in Irish city (6)

indicators.note: take the first letter of GUINNESS
drop the last letter of ALWAYS

explanation.surface: In an Irish city, you are nearly always served a Guinness first.
explanation.walkthrough: Galway is a city on the west coast of Ireland; Guinness is the Irish stout.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the city on Ireland's west coast is one of many Irish cities.

clue.text: Part of shop restocked quickly (6)

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the letters that follow

blocks.note: the six letters run from the end of SHOP into the start of RESTOCKED

explanation.surface: One section of a shop had its shelves refilled in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: Presto is the musical direction for a fast tempo, and a conjuror's word for instant magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto means quickly, as a tempo marking or in "hey presto".

clue.text: Tech data vigorously secured (8)

indicators.note: the letters are shaken up hard into a new order

explanation.surface: Technical data has been locked down with great energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The IT-security picture makes "secured" read as protected; here it means fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thing fixed firmly in place has been fastened on.

clue.text: Naturally spending time in a nice way (11)

indicators.note: CONGENITALLY spends, gives up, its T

explanation.surface: Being naturally inclined to use one's time pleasantly.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spending time" reads as passing time, but here it means losing a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenially means in a pleasant, agreeable, nice way.

clue.text: Fashion folk surrounded by alcohol and flowers (6-2-4)

indicators.note: something surrounded by another is enclosed on all sides, so the folk go inside the drinks

blocks.note: tots are small measures of spirits

explanation.surface: Fashionable people at a party, surrounded by drinks and bouquets.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fashion folk" reads as a single phrase for models and designers, but the two words do separate jobs; a tot is a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the little blue-flowered plant is one kind of flower.

clue.text: Unkind trick reported in the interim (9)

indicators.note: what is said, not written, gives the second part

explanation.surface: A nasty prank was mentioned while waiting for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: WILE and WHILE sound the same in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile means in the interim, during the time between.

clue.text: Californian opera company headed by investor (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, ANGEL sits at the head, above ENO

blocks.note: an angel is a backer of a stage show

explanation.surface: A Californian opera house is run by its main financial backer.
explanation.walkthrough: An Angeleno is a person from Los Angeles; the ENO is London's English National Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno, a native of Los Angeles, is a Californian.

clue.text: Changed tune to accept an apostate back, showing no repentance (12)

indicators.note: the letters of TUNE are changed around
the rearranged TUNE takes the rest inside
A RENEGER is read backwards

blocks.note: a reneger goes back on a promise or faith

explanation.surface: A song was rewritten to welcome back a defector who is not sorry at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious apostate is RENEGADE, but its D will not fit; RENEGER, one who reneges, is the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unregenerate means unreformed, not repenting of one's sins.

clue.text: Old mare roaming noble lands (7)

indicators.note: the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: An aged horse wanders across an aristocrat's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a horse loose on a country estate, which is exactly where the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the territory held by an earl, a noble's lands.

clue.text: Wild kid, full of spirit (6)

indicators.note: a thing full of something has it inside, so the teasing word is filled with the drink

blocks.note: to rag or kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: An unruly child is bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: "Kid" reads as a child, but it is the verb to tease; "spirit" reads as liveliness but is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging means wild, furious or out of control.

clue.text: Queen and soldiers backed man of steel (8)

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the soldiers are read right to left

blocks.note: REME = Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers

explanation.surface: A queen and her troops supported a superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: "Man of steel" suggests Superman; it is Henry Bessemer, whose converter made steel cheap. REME is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Bessemer invented the Bessemer process for making steel.

clue.text: Muslim leader turned amateur detective (5)

indicators.note: turned means faced about, so the amateur is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a ham is an amateur, as in ham radio

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader has taken up amateur sleuthing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mahdi is the redeemer expected in Islamic belief; the title was claimed by a Sudanese leader in the 1880s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mahdi is a prophesied Muslim leader, a title several rulers have claimed.

clue.text: Extremely wearisome St David’s Day in German city (6)

indicators.note: take the letters at the extremes of WEARISOME

blocks.note: first and last letters of WEARISOME
St David's Day is 1 March: I MAR

explanation.surface: St David's Day in a German city proves thoroughly tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: St David is the patron saint of Wales, celebrated on 1 March; the 1 becomes I and March is abbreviated MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Thuringian city of Goethe and the 1919 republic is one German city.

clue.text: Egyptian peasant collapsed with expression of surprise (6)

explanation.surface: An Egyptian farmworker fell down, crying out in astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: A fellah is a peasant farmer in Egypt and other Arab countries; the plural is fellahin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellah is the Arabic word for a peasant or agricultural labourer.

clue.text: Caustic story on the radio (3)

definitions.note: Caustic is an adjective; LYE is the noun for a caustic substance.

indicators.note: heard, not seen, so the spelling changes

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A cutting tale was broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: "Caustic" reads as an adjective for a sharp remark; lye is the caustic alkali, noun used as a modifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Lye is a strongly caustic alkaline solution, such as sodium hydroxide.

clue.text: Boring head of school snapped (5,3)

explanation.surface: A dull headteacher lost their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boring head" looks like a dull headteacher, but it is the cutting end of a drill, which bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill bit is the cutting head fitted to a drill for boring holes.

clue.text: Impropriety in exclusive clubs is essentially unlimited (8)

indicators.note: take the essence, the middle letter, of UNLIMITED

blocks.note: sole = exclusive, as in sole rights
M is the middle of the nine letters of UNLIMITED

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour in private members' clubs knows no bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: "Exclusive clubs" reads as one phrase for posh gentlemen's clubs; it splits into SOLE and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a breach of good manners or grammar, an impropriety.

clue.text: Plant at last made popular by the RHS? (6)

indicators.note: take the last letter of each of the next three words

blocks.note: last letters of MADE, POPULAR and BY
the RHS is a charity, a non-governmental organisation

explanation.surface: A plant has finally been made fashionable by the Royal Horticultural Society.
explanation.walkthrough: The RHS (Royal Horticultural Society) is Britain's gardening charity; the question mark flags it as one example of an NGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eryngo is sea holly, a spiky blue-flowered plant.
